title: John Gould, a violinist who played by ear
summary: He admired Gould, a Black violinist who played with guitar and bass trio and never read music, whom he heard when he was about 19-20.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: You told me the other day about hearing a violin player named John Gould. John Gould, yeah.

That's a nigga. Could you tell us a little bit about your son? I told you that and I meant that. And that nigga, I swear, I could sit down all night and listen at him play violin. Really good, isn't it?

That nigga could play a violin. Did he read? Huh? Did he read? No, he never read. He was a faker? Faker. And he had, Alderman Mitchell used to play guitar with him, and Henry Ford used to play bass. And he used to take different jobs, this fella Johnny Gould, you know, to play house for it. And that was all his band, three pieces, violin, guitar and bass. But he used to play plenty of jobs. When was that?
How old were you? Were you started on the carnet then?
Oh, I must have been about 19, 20 years of age. About that time? Yeah. That was shortly before, I think that I got started with music.
And they played at just private parties mostly, or did they play at any public places too?
